# Bornholm: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge

Bornholm: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge is a child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinic (børne- og ungdomspsykiatrisk ambulatorium) on the island of Bornholm, Denmark. It appears repeatedly in the annual reports of the Danish ADHD-databasen (ADHD database), a national quality-monitoring register that tracks how ADHD diagnostic and treatment pathways are carried out across Danish regions and departments [^src1] [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11]. The clinic is administratively part of, and located within, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] [^src1] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11], which places it within the wider network of psychiatric services covered by the ADHD database.

The clinic's performance is documented across two consecutive reporting periods. In the ADHD_2023 report, covering the period 01.04.2023–31.03.2024, Bornholm: Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge opnåede 28 % opfyldelse af Indikator 3 blandt 112 udredningsforløb [^src3], with 31 of 112 cases meeting the criterion (95 % CI: 20–37) [^src3]. This sits close to the national average for Indikator 3, which the broader dataset places at 21 % fulfilment, far below the 90 % development target set for Danish psychiatric departments [^src3]. The clinic also reported that 23 of 112 pathways (21 %) included somatic assessment [^src10], and recorded 0 % compliance for clinical environmental observation among 7 pathways, with a wide confidence interval of 0 (0–41) reflecting the very small sample size [^src11].

Performance on other indicators in the same 2023 report period was markedly lower. Bornholm havde 5 % opfyldelse af indikator 4 (95% CI: 1-15) med 3 forløb ud af 57 [^src1]. A related metric on page 32 of the same report similarly shows 4 of 57 pathways (7 %, CI 2–17) meeting a related criterion, again marked "Nej" (No) against the standard [^src2]. These figures are consistent with the report's broader finding that Indikator 4 and Indikator 5 (psychoeducation), both introduced on 25 May 2021, remain far below their 90 % targets nationally, reflecting a heavily burdened child and adolescent psychiatric system with long waiting times where treatment measures like psychoeducation and cross-sector coordination have been deprioritised in favour of diagnostic assessment [^src1] [^src2].

The subsequent ADHD_2024 report, covering 01.04.2024–31.03.2025, shows a shift in the clinic's data as it is listed under the code "Psykiatrisk ambulatorium, børn og unge, Bornh, B37." On Indikator 2b (manualised diagnostic interview or environmental observation), the clinic reported 40 of 79 pathways (51 %, CI 39–62) [^src4] — matching the national average of 51 % fulfilment reported for this indicator in 2024. On Indikator 3, performance dipped to 28 of 86 pathways (33 %, CI 23–44) [^src5], while a related metric shows only 3 of 86 pathways (3 %, CI 1–10) [^src6]. Further data points in the same period show 32 of 86 pathways (37 %, CI 27–48) [^src7] and, notably, 74 of 86 pathways (86 %, CI 77–93) on another metric marked with a 0 (0) qualifier [^src7], indicating strong performance on at least one measured dimension despite persistent shortfalls elsewhere. A separate entry lists a raw count of 17 for the clinic in an appendix table on demographic or population data [^src8].

Taken together, the record shows a small island-based clinic operating under [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] that, across two reporting years, consistently fell short of the Danish healthcare system's 90 % development targets on most ADHD quality indicators — particularly network coordination and psychoeducation — while showing comparatively stronger results on diagnostic interview/environmental observation measures by 2024. The broader ADHD-databasen context notes that national reviewers cited pressure on specialised psychiatry, geographic challenges, and competing priorities as drivers of low performance across departments like this one, prompting the steering group behind the database to revise several indicators, including shifting the network-meeting indicator toward contact with a patient's home municipality within 120 days of assessment start [^src1] [^src2].
